title.en: You can sign in on Microsoft's real page and still let a criminal into your inbox.
title.zh: 你登的是真微软，放进邮箱的却可能是骗子。

summary.en: Microsoft links EvilTokens to over 12,000 compromised inboxes across more than 10,000 organizations. One trick was to make a genuine sign-in approve the attacker's access.
summary.zh: 微软称，EvilTokens涉及1.2万多个被入侵邮箱，遍布1万多家机构。其中一招，是诱使用户在真正的登录页面上替攻击者批准访问。

en: The sign-in page can be genuine while the request behind it belongs to a criminal. Microsoft's September 22 report describes EvilTokens lures that led people to its real login page, where their approval authorized an attacker's session. Microsoft links the service as a whole to more than 12,000 compromised inboxes across over 10,000 organizations worldwide.

The abused feature was built for devices such as smart TVs and printers: you approve one device's access from another. A phishing message can disguise whose request you are approving. The victim's password need never reach the criminal. The report describes deception around authorization, rather than a break in MFA's cryptography; Microsoft continues to recommend MFA.

An exposed inbox then gave the service's AI tools material to analyze. Microsoft says they could identify payment conversations and trusted relationships, helping criminals choose whom to impersonate. That is why an unusual payment request deserves a separate check, even when it comes from a familiar mailbox. The technical report also describes malicious inbox rules that concealed communications.

EvilTokens emerged in February 2026. On September 22, Microsoft announced that it and partners had seized 50 websites and disabled more than 150 supporting domains. That disrupts infrastructure; it does not establish that every compromised account is safe. Microsoft warns that access can survive a password reset when associated sessions and tokens remain valid. The DCU describes a business with customer support, a $1,500 entry fee and a $500 monthly subscription.

For readers, the useful check is what access a sign-in is approving and whether you initiated it. For organizations, Microsoft's guidance is to review the need for device-code login, block it where possible, and keep necessary exceptions narrow. Requests to redirect payments should be verified through a trusted second channel.
zh: 登录页面可以是真的，背后的请求却可能属于骗子。微软9月22日发布的报告描述了EvilTokens的一种骗术：把用户引到真正的微软登录页，再让用户的确认替攻击者批准访问。微软称，整个服务涉及全球1万多家机构、1.2万多个被入侵邮箱。
被滥用的功能原本方便电视、打印机等设备登录：你在另一台设备上批准它的访问请求。钓鱼消息把“到底在批准谁”藏了起来，攻击者甚至不必拿到你的密码。报告描述的是授权过程中的欺骗，没有证据表明MFA的加密机制被破解；微软仍建议使用MFA。
邮箱一旦失守，里面的往来就成了AI工具的分析材料。微软称，这些工具能找出付款讨论和信任关系，帮助骗子挑选冒充对象。所以，即使改收款账户的消息来自熟悉的邮箱，也应该换一个可信渠道核实。 技术报告还记录了另一种掩饰：设置恶意收件规则，把相关邮件藏起来。
EvilTokens在2026年2月出现。微软9月22日宣布，已与合作方查封50个网站，并停用150多个配套域名。这是对基础设施的打击，不能据此认定所有被入侵账户都已安全。微软还提醒：如果相关会话和令牌仍然有效，只改密码，攻击者的访问权限可能还在。 按微软DCU的描述，这门生意还配客服：入门费1,500美元，每月再收500美元。
读者需要看清的是：这次登录在批准什么访问，是不是自己发起的。机构则应按微软建议，检查是否需要设备代码登录，能禁用就禁用，必要例外尽量收窄。遇到更改付款信息的请求，用另一个可信渠道确认。

wtf.en: The genuine login can complete the fraud: the user approves access for the wrong session.
wtf.zh: 真正的登录页也能完成骗术：用户批准的，可能是攻击者那边的访问。

consequence.en: A compromised inbox can expose both private messages and the relationships that make the next fraud attempt convincing.
consequence.zh: 邮箱失守，泄露的不只是邮件，还有让下一次冒充更可信的人际关系。

uncertainty.en: The compromise counts and disruption results are Microsoft's account, not an independent census. They cover EvilTokens as a service, not a verified total for device-code phishing alone. September 22 is the report and announcement date; the service emerged in February. Disruption does not prove eradication or complete account recovery. There is no evidence here of a cryptographic MFA break.
uncertainty.zh: 入侵规模和打击结果来自微软通报，并非独立普查。这些数字覆盖整个EvilTokens服务，不能全部归到设备代码钓鱼这一招上。9月22日是报告及公告日期，服务在2月已经出现。打击基础设施不等于彻底清除威胁，也不等于所有账户已恢复安全。现有材料没有证明MFA的加密机制被破解。

sources.title: Microsoft Digital Crimes Unit: Disrupting EvilTokens
Microsoft Learn: OAuth device authorization grant
Microsoft Learn: Restrict device code authentication flows

claims.text: Microsoft reports that EvilTokens lures directed users to its genuine sign-in portal, where approval could authorize an attacker session without exposing the victim password. A genuine domain alone does not validate the authorization request.

Microsoft links EvilTokens as a service to more than 12,000 compromised inboxes across over 10,000 organizations worldwide; these are attributed service-wide counts, not a count confined to one attack technique.
Microsoft says EvilTokens emerged in February 2026. Its technical report and disruption announcement were published September 22, 2026.
Legitimate device authorization lets users approve access for devices with limited input, including smart TVs and printers, through a browser on another device.
Microsoft describes abuse of authorization/session context to circumvent traditional MFA protections. It does not report a cryptographic break in MFA, and still recommends MFA.

Microsoft says EvilTokens AI tools could analyze compromised inboxes, identify financial conversations and trusted relationships, and help criminals choose impersonation targets. These are reported capabilities, not proof that AI caused every compromise.

Microsoft says it and partners seized 50 websites and disabled more than 150 supporting domains. Infrastructure disruption does not establish that the service model disappeared or every account recovered.
Microsoft warns that access could persist after a password reset if associated sessions and tokens were not revoked.
Microsoft recommends auditing device code flow usage, blocking it where possible, and restricting necessary exceptions. Legitimate uses exist.
Microsoft recommends independently verifying payment changes or unusual transactions through a trusted second channel.
Microsoft reports AI capabilities for tailoring lures to target roles and analyzing mailbox content after compromise; later messages can exploit existing trusted contacts.
Microsoft reports use of malicious inbox rules to conceal communications and retain access, with behavior varying between incidents.

Microsoft DCU reports EvilTokens was sold for a $1,500 initiation fee and a $500 recurring subscription, with customer support and a management interface. The technical report specifies the subscription as monthly.

experiment.hypothesis: Test the trusted-login reversal against the attributed service-wide compromise count. Both promises are paid off in the first paragraph; body, artwork, placement and render version stay fixed. Editorial scores are untested preferences, not observed performance. Judge qualified consumption per exposure with misleading/hide feedback at the scheduled review; insufficient observations remain UNKNOWN.

hooks.en: You can sign in on Microsoft's real page and still let a criminal into your inbox.
hooks.zh: 你登的是真微软，放进邮箱的却可能是骗子。
hooks.reader_promise: Explain how an authentic page can approve hostile access.
hooks.payoff: The sign-in is genuine; the session it approves can belong to the attacker.
hooks.risk: Could imply every Microsoft login is unsafe; keep the conditional and identify the deceptive request.

hooks.en: Microsoft: one phishing service, over 12,000 inboxes compromised.
hooks.zh: 微软：一个钓鱼服务，涉及1.2万多个被入侵邮箱。
hooks.reader_promise: Show the measured scope claimed by the investigator.
hooks.payoff: Microsoft links the service to 12,000-plus inboxes across 10,000-plus organizations.
hooks.risk: Counts are attributed and service-wide, not independently audited or all due to one technique.

hooks.en: A criminal can get into your inbox without ever seeing your password.
hooks.zh: 骗子没见过你的密码，也可能进了你的邮箱。
hooks.reader_promise: Reveal access without password disclosure.
hooks.payoff: The victim can approve an attacker session through a legitimate sign-in.
hooks.risk: Must not suggest all account access works this way or that passwords no longer matter.

hooks.angle: reversal: normal check can be insufficient
hooks.en: The web address checks out. The access request still needs checking.
hooks.zh: 网址查了，是真的。访问请求是谁的，还得再看。
hooks.reader_promise: Add a practical check beyond domain inspection.
hooks.payoff: EvilTokens used a genuine portal to approve a request initiated by an attacker.
hooks.risk: Do not discourage checking URLs; explain why it is insufficient by itself.

hooks.angle: reversal: recovery can leave access alive
hooks.en: You changed the password. An attacker could still have inbox access.
hooks.zh: 密码改了，攻击者却可能还留在邮箱里。
hooks.reader_promise: Explain the recovery gap.
hooks.payoff: Microsoft warns that surviving sessions and tokens can preserve access after a reset.
hooks.risk: Conditional on sessions/tokens remaining valid; never imply password resets are useless.

hooks.en: A familiar email address can carry somebody else's payment instructions.
hooks.zh: 熟悉的邮箱地址，发来的可能是骗子的付款指令。
hooks.reader_promise: Explain why a trusted sender is insufficient for payment changes.
hooks.payoff: Compromised mailboxes and relationship analysis can help criminals impersonate trusted contacts.
hooks.risk: This is a capability and risk, not an invented named victim or verified loss.

hooks.en: Your inbox tells a thief whom you trust. Microsoft says AI can help read it.
hooks.zh: 邮箱会告诉骗子你信谁。微软说，AI能帮他们读出来。
hooks.reader_promise: Show what stolen correspondence reveals.
hooks.payoff: Microsoft describes tools that identify trusted relationships and impersonation targets.
hooks.risk: AI capability must remain attributed; do not assume every stolen inbox was analyzed.

hooks.en: Who can approve a payment? Microsoft says this crime service could find out from emails.
hooks.zh: 谁能批付款？微软称，这个犯罪服务能从邮件里找线索。
hooks.reader_promise: Connect mailbox access to financial decision makers.
hooks.payoff: The tools could surface financial conversations and identify targets for impersonation.
hooks.risk: Finding clues is not proof that payments were diverted in every case.

hooks.en: Your inbox can be compromised while rules hide the suspicious mail.
hooks.zh: 邮箱可能已经失守，可疑邮件还被规则藏了起来。
hooks.reader_promise: Explain why the visible inbox may omit warning signs.
hooks.payoff: Microsoft reports malicious inbox rules that concealed communications.
hooks.risk: An observed behavior in some incidents, not an assertion about every victim.

hooks.en: The attacker needs your approval. The trick is hiding whose access you approve.
hooks.zh: 攻击者要的是你的批准。骗术在于，让你看不清批准的是谁。
hooks.reader_promise: Make the authorization mistake legible.
hooks.payoff: A device-code lure can make a genuine sign-in authorize the wrong session.
hooks.risk: Do not provide an attack recipe or imply accidental approval is inevitable.

hooks.angle: mechanism: a feature built for televisions
hooks.en: A login feature built for TVs and printers became a route into work inboxes.
hooks.zh: 本来方便电视、打印机登录的功能，被拿来闯进工作邮箱。
hooks.reader_promise: Explain the legitimate feature behind the abuse.
hooks.payoff: Device authorization lets one device approve another; phishing can substitute the attacker request.
hooks.risk: The feature has legitimate uses; abuse does not prove every deployment is vulnerable.

hooks.en: Once inside an inbox, EvilTokens offered AI help choosing the next person to impersonate.
hooks.zh: 钻进邮箱后，EvilTokens还能用AI帮骗子挑下一个冒充对象。
hooks.reader_promise: Show the post-compromise role of AI.
hooks.payoff: Microsoft describes relationship analysis and suggested impersonation targets.
hooks.risk: Reported platform capability, not independently measured effectiveness.

hooks.en: MFA can check your identity while a deceptive request gets your approval.
hooks.zh: MFA确认了你是谁，骗人的访问请求却仍可能得到你的批准。
hooks.reader_promise: Explain why authentication and authorization context both matter.
hooks.payoff: Microsoft describes a legitimate sign-in approving an attacker session and still recommends MFA.
hooks.risk: Must not suggest a cryptographic break or advise disabling MFA.

hooks.en: Over 10,000 organizations, Microsoft says. One service sold the phishing tools.
hooks.zh: 微软称，涉及1万多家机构。背后是同一个钓鱼工具服务。
hooks.reader_promise: Show organizational reach while keeping attribution.
hooks.payoff: The reported service-wide count spans more than 10,000 organizations.
hooks.risk: Organization count is not the number of complete corporate network takeovers.

hooks.en: Microsoft says it seized 50 EvilTokens sites. That cannot certify every inbox safe.
hooks.zh: 微软称查封了50个EvilTokens网站。每个邮箱都安全了吗？还不能这么说。
hooks.reader_promise: Separate a major intervention from individual recovery.
hooks.payoff: The operation disrupted infrastructure; account recovery is a separate unresolved question.
hooks.risk: Do not imply a failed operation merely because eradication is unproven.

hooks.en: EvilTokens surfaced in February. Microsoft now reports more than 12,000 breached inboxes.
hooks.zh: EvilTokens在2月出现。如今微软披露：被入侵邮箱超过1.2万个。
hooks.reader_promise: Give the timeline behind the September announcement.
hooks.payoff: September 22 brings a new report on a service that emerged in February.
hooks.risk: No invented monthly growth rate or claim that every compromise occurred in September.

hooks.en: Does your company need device-code login? Microsoft says to block it where possible.
hooks.zh: 公司真需要设备代码登录吗？微软建议：能禁用就禁用。
hooks.reader_promise: Offer a concrete organizational decision.
hooks.payoff: Audit legitimate use, then restrict the flow and narrowly scope necessary exceptions.
hooks.risk: Avoid blanket advice that could break necessary device access.

hooks.en: Before changing bank details, check through a channel the mailbox thief does not control.
hooks.zh: 改收款账户之前，换个邮箱窃贼管不到的渠道确认。
hooks.reader_promise: Give a practical consequence for payment workflows.
hooks.payoff: Microsoft recommends a trusted second channel for changed payment instructions.
hooks.risk: Editorial plain-language advice, not a claim of guaranteed protection.

hooks.angle: business model: subscription and customer support
hooks.en: Microsoft: inbox theft came with a monthly bill and customer support.
hooks.zh: 微软：偷邮箱，也做成了包月服务，还配客服。
hooks.reader_promise: Show how the service packaged cybercrime as a subscription business.
hooks.payoff: The DCU describes customer support, a $1,500 entry fee and a $500 recurring subscription; the technical report specifies monthly.
hooks.risk: Reported business model, not proof that every paying subscriber succeeded or that these were the only costs.

hooks.en: Before you approve a login, check who started it. The real page cannot answer for you.
hooks.zh: 确认登录前，先看是不是自己发起的。页面是真的，也不能替你做这个判断。
hooks.reader_promise: Turn the reversal into an immediately usable question.
hooks.payoff: A genuine page may be approving access requested by somebody else.
hooks.risk: Do not claim user vigilance alone replaces organizational controls.

title.en: Scientists expected lake sediment. Mars handed them rock born from magma.
title.zh: 科学家等着看古湖沉积物，火星交出的却是岩浆冷却成的岩石。

summary.en: The unexpected rocks preserve at least three ancient encounters with water. Scientists can order them, but cannot yet date them.
summary.zh: 更意外的是，这批岩石留下了至少三轮古老水活动的痕迹。先后顺序能排出来，具体年代还不知道。

en: Scientists expected lake sediments along an ancient shoreline in Jezero Crater. Perseverance found rock formed from magma instead. Those rocks preserve evidence of at least three separate episodes of interaction with water.

The rover reached this area, the Margin Unit, in September 2023. The study published on September 21, 2026 draws on SuperCam measurements of more than 185 bedrock targets. Its laser can examine rock from up to 6.5 metres away.

First, groundwater rich in carbon dioxide left carbonate in fractures. A later episode involved either lake water or changes in groundwater, leaving further alterations including silica. Eventually, heated underground water deposited mineral veins containing fluorite and calcium sulfate.

The team can reconstruct the sequence, but the episodes' absolute ages remain unknown. These changing environments give researchers more to investigate about ancient habitability. The study reports mineral evidence of water activity, with no discovery of life.
zh: 科学家原本期待在耶泽罗陨石坑的古湖岸边看到沉积岩。毅力号看到的却是岩浆形成的岩石。更出乎意料的是，这批岩石保存了至少三轮与水发生作用的痕迹。
毅力号早在2023年9月就抵达这片“边缘单元”。2026年9月21日发表的新研究分析了SuperCam对185多个基岩目标的测量；它的激光最远能在6.5米外分析岩石。
最初，富含二氧化碳的地下水在岩石裂缝里留下碳酸盐。后来一轮变化可能来自湖水，也可能来自地下水条件的改变，留下了二氧化硅等痕迹。再后来，受热地下水带来了含萤石和硫酸钙的矿脉。
研究人员能排出这些变化的先后，却还不知道它们各自发生在哪个年代。这些不同环境为研究远古火星是否适宜生命提供了线索；本次发现的是水活动的矿物证据，没有发现生命。

wtf.en: The rocks that upset the lake-sediment expectation turned out to preserve several chapters of Mars' water history.
wtf.zh: 没找到预想的湖岸沉积岩，却从火成岩里读出了至少三轮水活动。

consequence.en: Researchers now have several successive water environments to reconstruct when assessing this site's ancient habitability.
consequence.zh: 判断这片地方远古时是否适宜生命，需要弄清多轮水活动各自形成的环境。

uncertainty.en: The episodes' absolute ages are unknown. Lake involvement in the second episode is one explanation, alongside changed groundwater. These are ancient mineral traces, not evidence of present liquid water or a discovery of life.
uncertainty.zh: 各轮活动的绝对年代未知。第二轮可能涉及湖水，也可能是地下水条件变化。这些是古老矿物痕迹，不能说发现了现存液态水或生命。

sources.title: NASA: Complex water systems recorded in early Mars rocks
Bedford et al.: Lake- and groundwater-associated alteration of the olivine-rich Margin unit

claims.text: The team expected sedimentary rocks near an ancient Jezero lake shoreline; Perseverance reached the Margin Unit in September2023.
The study interprets the unit as originally crystalline igneous rock; some exposures also show sedimentary reworking. High-elevation rocks are consistent with slow cooling of magma underground.
The rocks preserve evidence of at least three separate episodes of water-rock interaction.
The first episode involved CO2-rich groundwater and carbonate precipitation in bedrock fractures.
The second episode may reflect lake-water exposure or changes in groundwater; carbonate moved and silica precipitated.
Later heated underground fluids deposited fluorite-bearing calcium-sulfate veins in fractures.
The team can determine the sequence of water interactions, but their absolute ages remain unknown.
SuperCam measured more than185 bedrock targets across the unit; its laser operates at distances up to6.5metres.
The study identifies environments of astrobiological interest through ancient water-rock alteration; it does not report a discovery of life or present liquid water.
NASA's report and the research paper were published September21,2026; this is the report date, not a new rover arrival.

title.en: FF launches nine robots. Its own warning says it cannot pay outstanding obligations.

summary.en: Nine new devices, a funding warning and a supply chain still tied to Chinese manufacturers.

en: Nine new robots, two unresolved problems. FF discloses that it currently cannot pay outstanding obligations, and all its robotics products depend on Chinese manufacturers. Its US production program targets future generations. The financial warning predates this launch.

Faraday Future’s September 20 release says the new lineup starts at $9,990 and is available for immediate delivery. The launch brings new products; it does not establish that funding or supplier dependence has been resolved.

The lineup spans $9,990–$137,900, targeting schools, research, security and inspection. FF reports 552 units in cumulative sales and shipments through August. Most robotics products rely on one manufacturer; tariffs and possible import restrictions feature among the risks.

The next US manufacturing partner event is scheduled for September 28. Watch for actual funding and production changes. The current dependence is not evidence of a broken future manufacturing promise.

summary.en: An astronomer’s estimate for Roman’s planned survey. Hubble’s famous images cover just 0.1% of the sky.

en: Half a million 4K TVs. That is astronomer David Weinberg’s estimate for displaying Roman’s entire planned high-latitude survey at full resolution. The map has not been made yet.

NASA says Hubble has seen just 0.1% of the sky in more than three decades. Roman launched on August 30 with the same primary-mirror diameter, but its wide-field instrument covers roughly 100 times more sky per image.

The planned survey should capture over a billion galaxies to help investigate dark matter and accelerating cosmic expansion. First images were forecast for early 2027. A vast field of view is ready; the evidence still has to arrive.

title.en: Claude’s maker wants outsiders to inspect its AI. It will pay them.
title.zh: Claude 的开发者要请人查自己。钱，自己出。

summary.en: Anthropic will fund Accenture’s work directly. How much its watchdogs can see—and report—is still being worked out.
summary.zh: Anthropic 将直接付钱给埃森哲做评估。监督者能查多深、能公开什么，标准仍未敲定。

en: Anthropic plans to bring outsiders into the company to inspect its AI—and pay them itself. Its September 18 announcement says it will directly fund Accenture’s embedded evaluation work.

Each company expects to invest at least $1 billion over five years in this capability. Access and reporting standards remain unsettled. Dario Amodei proposes allowing unfavorable findings to be published, with specified redactions.
The funding is clear. The test comes when a finding makes the payer uncomfortable: does the public still get to read it?

两家公司各自预计在五年内投入至少10亿美元建设相关能力。监督者能看到哪些内部资料、如何报告发现，尚无统一标准。Dario Amodei 提出的合同方案允许公开不利结论，但保留特定删节权。
钱由谁出，已经说清。要等实际执行回答的是：如果报告让付款方难堪，公众还能照样读到吗？

title.en: You never gave away your password. One approval can still let an attacker in.
title.zh: 密码没交出去，点个批准，黑客却可能进了公司账户。

summary.en: Investigators found hotel-network redirects that could turn a routine sign-in approval into access for an attacker.
summary.zh: 调查人员发现，有酒店网络把住客引向授权陷阱：你点批准，对方拿到公司账户的访问令牌。

en: You do not have to hand over your password. ReliaQuest documented hotel-network redirects that could trick travelers into approving a sign-in session started by an attacker. The approval sends valid access tokens to the attacker’s client.

Anthropic’s September 10 report says an espionage operator compromised at least three hotel Wi-Fi suppliers. Microsoft had reported the associated CaptiveCrunch campaign in July, including fake-update lures and AI-assisted operations. The reports describe several tactics, not one identical attack against every guest.

Merely joining Wi-Fi does not prove your account was compromised. The device-code trick needs the user’s approval—and a genuine sign-in page can still authorize the wrong party, as separate Volexity cases from 2025 showed.
zh: 密码没有交出去，也可能替黑客开了门。ReliaQuest 记录的部分酒店网络攻击，会把旅客引向授权提示。你一旦批准，攻击者发起的会话就能拿到有效访问令牌。
Anthropic 9月10日的报告称，一名间谍行动操作者攻陷了至少三家酒店 Wi-Fi 服务商。微软此前在7月披露相关的 CaptiveCrunch 行动，包括假更新诱饵和 AI 辅助操作。这些报告描述了多种手法，并非每位住客都遭遇同一套攻击。
仅仅连接 Wi-Fi，不代表账户就被攻陷。设备代码骗局还需要骗到你的批准。Volexity 在另一些2025年案例中也记录过：登录页可以是真的，但你授权登录的人，可能不是你自己。

wtf.en: The trick needs your approval, not necessarily your password.
wtf.zh: 这种骗局要骗到的，是你的批准；不一定是密码。

consequence.en: The office perimeter travels with its people.
consequence.zh: 员工走到哪里，公司的安全边界就延伸到哪里。

uncertainty.en: Vendor investigations; current campaign activity is unverified. Affected networks are not all hotel networks.
uncertainty.zh: 依据安全厂商调查；行动目前是否仍在进行，未验证。受影响网络不等于所有酒店网络。

claims.text: Anthropic reports at least three compromised hotel Wi-Fi suppliers and combined guest/device data used for targeting.
Microsoft reports AI-assisted CaptiveCrunch activity, fake-update malware lures, and attribution to a Midnight Blizzard sub-cluster.
ReliaQuest observed hotel-network redirects, account-authorization lures without phishing email, and attacks on traveling corporate staff.
Separate Volexity cases from 2025 used genuine Microsoft device-code pages to trick users into authorizing attacker access.
Device-code authorization is a legitimate sign-in flow in which user approval enables the requesting application to receive tokens.

ReliaQuest reports limited cases pairing hotel-network redirects with device-code abuse: approving the prompt gives the attacker-controlled client valid OAuth tokens, without collecting the password on a fake page.

hooks.zh: 密码没交出去，点个批准，黑客却可能进了公司账户。
hooks.en: You never gave away your password. One approval can still let an attacker in.

hooks.zh: 酒店 Wi-Fi 弹出的登录提示，可能在替黑客要你的批准。
hooks.en: That sign-in prompt on hotel Wi-Fi may be asking you to authorize an attacker.

hooks.zh: 你以为在给自己登录，那个批准却可能是给黑客的。
hooks.en: You think you are signing yourself in. The approval may belong to an attacker.

hooks.zh: 没钓鱼邮件，也没点陌生链接，酒店网照样能把人送进陷阱。
hooks.en: No phishing email. No strange link. A compromised hotel network can deliver the trap.

hooks.zh: 你在酒店连 Wi-Fi，对方盯的却是你的公司账户。
hooks.en: You join the hotel Wi-Fi. The attacker is after your work account.

hooks.zh: 真正危险的，可能是登录页上那次亲手点下的批准。
hooks.en: The dangerous click can be your approval on a sign-in page.

hooks.zh: 至少三家酒店 Wi-Fi 服务商被攻陷，住客成了筛选目标。
hooks.en: At least three hotel Wi-Fi vendors were compromised, Anthropic reports. Guests became targets.

hooks.zh: 酒店网让你更新软件？微软披露的诱饵就长这样。
hooks.en: A software update on hotel Wi-Fi? Microsoft documented that malware lure.

hooks.zh: 不偷密码，骗你授权：酒店网络攻击走了另一扇门。
hooks.en: No stolen password needed: hotel-network attackers tricked users into authorizing access.

hooks.zh: 连上酒店网后，熟悉的微软登录也可能被拿来做局。
hooks.en: On a compromised hotel network, a familiar Microsoft sign-in can become the lure.

hooks.zh: 登录页是真的，也挡不住你把权限给错人。
hooks.en: A real sign-in page cannot stop you from authorizing the wrong party.

hooks.zh: 出差的人换了酒店，公司的账户也跟着暴露在新的风险里。
hooks.en: The employee changes hotels. The work account enters a new risk zone.

hooks.zh: 黑客要找住客，先拿下了给酒店供网的人。
hooks.en: To reach hotel guests, the attacker went after the Wi-Fi suppliers.

hooks.zh: 住客名单加上设备信息，成了间谍筛人的线索。
hooks.en: Guest records plus device data became an espionage targeting tool.

hooks.zh: 酒店里的不速之客，可能藏在登录流程里。
hooks.en: The unwelcome guest may be hiding in the hotel’s sign-in flow.

hooks.zh: 点完批准，令牌发给谁？这才是酒店登录骗局的机关。
hooks.en: You approve the prompt. Who gets the token? That is the hotel sign-in trap.

hooks.zh: 微软披露：针对旅客的网络攻击，也用上了 AI。
hooks.en: Microsoft says AI helped a campaign targeting travelers.

hooks.zh: 以为给电脑打补丁，等着你的却可能是恶意软件。
hooks.en: You think you are patching your computer. The update may be malware.

hooks.zh: 设备代码骗局早就出现过，酒店网又给它开了一道门。
hooks.en: Device-code phishing was already here. Hotel networks gave it another doorway.

hooks.zh: 下一次出差，最该看清的也许是你在替谁批准登录。
hooks.en: On your next work trip, check whose sign-in you are approving.

linkedin.en:
That sign-in prompt on hotel Wi-Fi may be asking you to authorize an attacker.

Investigators found hotel-network redirects that could turn a routine sign-in approval into access for an attacker.

Merely joining Wi-Fi does not prove your account was compromised. The device-code trick needs the user’s approval—and a genuine sign-in page can still authorize the wrong party, as separate Volexity cases from 2025 showed.
linkedin.zh:
酒店 Wi-Fi 弹出的登录提示，可能在替黑客要你的批准。

调查人员发现，有酒店网络把住客引向授权陷阱：你点批准，对方拿到公司账户的访问令牌。

仅仅连接 Wi-Fi，不代表账户就被攻陷。设备代码骗局还需要骗到你的批准。Volexity 在另一些2025年案例中也记录过：登录页可以是真的，但你授权登录的人，可能不是你自己。

wechat.en:
You never gave away your password. One approval can still let an attacker in.

You do not have to hand over your password. ReliaQuest documented hotel-network redirects that could trick travelers into approving a sign-in session started by an attacker. The approval sends valid access tokens to the attacker’s client.

Anthropic’s September 10 report says an espionage operator compromised at least three hotel Wi-Fi suppliers. Microsoft had reported the associated CaptiveCrunch campaign in July, including fake-update lures and AI-assisted operations. The reports describe several tactics, not one identical attack against every guest.

Merely joining Wi-Fi does not prove your account was compromised. The device-code trick needs the user’s approval—and a genuine sign-in page can still authorize the wrong party, as separate Volexity cases from 2025 showed.
wechat.zh:
密码没交出去，点个批准，黑客却可能进了公司账户。

密码没有交出去，也可能替黑客开了门。ReliaQuest 记录的部分酒店网络攻击，会把旅客引向授权提示。你一旦批准，攻击者发起的会话就能拿到有效访问令牌。

Anthropic 9月10日的报告称，一名间谍行动操作者攻陷了至少三家酒店 Wi-Fi 服务商。微软此前在7月披露相关的 CaptiveCrunch 行动，包括假更新诱饵和 AI 辅助操作。这些报告描述了多种手法，并非每位住客都遭遇同一套攻击。
